question: If you skipped every haircut for a whole year, roughly how many centimetres longer would the hair on your head get?
source_excerpt: Human hair grows on average 1.25 centimetres (0.5 inches) per month, which is equivalent to about 15 centimetres (six inches) per year.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone has felt their hair outgrow a haircut, but few have added it up. Players can reason from 'about a centimetre a month' to a yearly figure, which makes a satisfying 'I worked it out' moment.
extra.verification_notes: Commonly cited average of ~1.25 cm/month gives ~15 cm/year (some sources say ~1 cm/month, ~12 cm), so 'roughly 15 cm' is acceptable; see https://www.sciencefocus.com/the-human-body/how-fast-does-hair-grow

explanation: Scalp hair grows a little over a centimetre a month, so a year adds about 15 cm, roughly the length of a pencil. That's why a fringe needs trimming every few weeks.

question: Your ten fingernails don't all grow at the same speed. On a typical hand, which finger's nail grows the fastest?
topic: How fast fingernails and hair grow
source_excerpt: the nail of the middle finger grows more rapidly than the nails of either the thumb or the little finger

extra.why_interesting: Players assume all ten nails grow at one shared speed, since they get trimmed together. Learning that each finger has its own rate, and that the rate roughly follows finger length, is a real 'huh, really?' moment. Players can also reason toward it by looking at their own hand.
extra.verification_notes: Sources, including a 35-year self-measurement study, report the middle finger's nail grows fastest and the little finger's slowest; no newer finding contradicts this.

explanation: As a rough rule, the longer the finger, the faster its nail grows, so the middle finger leads and the little finger trails behind. Nails on your dominant hand also tend to grow a little faster than those on the other hand.
